forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Ashfield council capital programme drives up debt charges to 15% of revenue by 2028–29
news_drafts.lead: Ashfield Council's £68.7m capital programme for 2026–27 will require £15.2m of new borrowing, increasing the proportion of its day-to-day revenue spent on financing debt from 11.31% this year to 15.07% by 2028–29. The Audit Committee heard that reduced government funding and rising Minimum Revenue Provision charges (the amount councils must set aside each year to repay past borrowing) will drive the increase. However, income from the council's investment properties materially offsets these costs, reducing the effective financing burden to 6.63% by 2028–29. The council has also tightened its borrowing policy, switching to a more prudent 50-year repayment method for pre-2008 debt instead of a schedule that would have extended over 300 years. PWLB borrowing rates fell slightly in the first quarter of 2026, from 5.62% to 5.55% on ten-year loans.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Treasury Management 2026/27 - Q1 April - June 2026
findings.headline: Minimum Revenue Provision policy for pre-2008 borrowing revised to 50-year annuity method, replacing 4% reducing balance approach which extended over 300 years
findings.detail: Council has adopted more prudent MRP methodology charging MRP on pre-2008 supported borrowing over 50-year annuity basis aligned to equivalent PWLB rate, rather than previous approach which would have extended amortisation beyond 300 years. Post-2008 borrowing uses annuity method for assets over 10 years life, straight-line for shorter-life assets.
findings.matters: More prudent MRP approach accelerates retirement of historic debt and improves long-term financial sustainability through faster de-leveraging
findings.figures: 50-year PWLB rate used for annuity calculation; straight-line method for assets under 10 years
findings.quote: For pre 2008 supported borrowing, the Council has moved to a 50-year Annuity method, charging MRP based on a corresponding 50-year PWLB borrowing rate. This is more prudent than the previous 4% reducing balance as this calculation extends to over 300 years.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Treasury Management 2026/27 - Q1 April - June 2026
findings.headline: PWLB 10-year rates fell from 5.62% (1 April) to 5.55% (30 June 2026); Bank Rate forecast to remain at 3.75% this year then fall to 3.25% by spring 2028
findings.detail: Gilt yields showed volatility in Q1, peaking at 5.18% in mid-May before falling to 4.76% by quarter end. MUFG forecasts Bank Rate at 3.75% through 2026, falling to 3.5% by end 2027, and 3.25% by spring 2028. Forecast assumes weak labour market and subdued growth will prevent second-round inflation effects.
findings.matters: Lower interest rate forecasts reduce expected cost of future borrowing; current quarter rates better than earlier in year, improving refinancing conditions
findings.figures: PWLB 10-year rate range Q1 2026: 5.50-5.98%; 1-year range 4.75-5.17%; 10-year average 5.71%
findings.quote: The 10-year Gilt yield has generally traced that move, falling back to 4.7% in June. This rally in Gilts has also been supported by the Bank of England keeping rates on hold

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Treasury Management 2026/27 - Q1 April - June 2026
findings.headline: Capital programme of £68.7m in 2026/27 requires £15.2m new borrowing; Capital Financing Requirement growing through 2029/30
findings.detail: Capital expenditure totals £68.7m in 2026/27 (£50.2m General Fund, £18.5m HRA). Unfinanced capital expenditure of £15.2m requires new borrowing. Capital Financing Requirement is forecast to grow from £175.4m (March 2026) to £176.5m (March 2030) before declining as Minimum Revenue Provision charges exceed new borrowing.
findings.matters: Demonstrates substantial sustained borrowing requirement extending over multiple years, progressively increasing council indebtedness
findings.figures: £68.701m total capital expenditure; £15.208m borrowing requirement (2026/27); CFR growth from £175.4m to £176.5m over four-year period
findings.quote: Table 3 below summarises how the capital expenditure plans will be financed by capital or revenue resources. Any shortfall of resources results in a borrowing need.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Treasury Management 2026/27 - Q1 April - June 2026
findings.headline: Investment property income offsets financing costs by 1.9-2.4 percentage points, materially supporting financial sustainability
findings.detail: Commercial property income reduces the financing cost burden from 11.31% to 9.45% in 2026/27, from 14.61% to 7.71% in 2027/28, and from 15.07% to 6.63% in 2028/29. Council financial viability depends materially on property valuations and rental yields continuing at current levels.
findings.matters: Council's financial sustainability is now contingent on continued commercial property performance; property market downturn or rental pressure would significantly worsen the underlying financing position
findings.figures: Financing costs reduced by 1.86pp (2026/27), 6.90pp (2027/28), 8.44pp (2028/29) when property income included
findings.quote: The investment properties have significant financing costs. However, these financing costs are significantly more than offset by the income they generate.

findings.paper_title: Enc. 1 for Treasury Management 2026/27 - Q1 April - June 2026
findings.headline: General Fund financing costs rising from 11.31% of net revenue (2026/27) to 15.07% by 2028/29
findings.detail: Capital programme investment is driving increasing debt service costs as a proportion of core council revenue. The ratio jumps from 11.31% (2026/27) to 14.61% (2027/28) and then to 15.07% (2028/29), reflecting both reduced government funding and rising Minimum Revenue Provision charges. This leaves progressively less revenue available for delivering services.
findings.matters: Rising debt service burden indicates tightening financial position and reduces financial flexibility; at 15%, financing costs consume a material portion of controllable revenue
findings.quote: The Ratio for the General Fund increases from 2027/28 as a result of reduced Government funding and increased MRP charges due to Capital Programme Developments.
